svg.title: Red eye: red flags decide whether it is vision threatening. Without them it is the lids, a conjunctivitis told apart by its discharge and itch, a subconjunctival hemorrhage or a corneal abrasion; with them it is keratitis, anterior uveitis or acute angle closure glaucoma and needs urgent ophthalmology; each column gives the presentation, the exam finding that decides it and the treatment

svg.text: Red eye: is it VISION THREATENING?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: red flag symptoms: blurred vision that does not clear with blinking · SEVERE pain · photophobia · coloured halos

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: red flag signs: ↓ acuity · ciliary flush · corneal opacity · abnormal pupil · shallow chamber · ↑ pressure · proptosis

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: ask: contact lenses (swim, sleep, shower in them?) · discharge · itch · recent cold · trauma

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: NO red flags: lids, conjunctiva, surface

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: acuity and pressure normal: treat or reassure
